A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SimScale. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original sim-real co-training experiments on navhard and navtest, including performance tables, scaling analyses, ablations and ensemble experiments.

after.justification: V2 retains original driving experiments and adds simulation-difficulty and visual-fidelity results, including Figure 8 and Table 10.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the perturbation condition from t = H to t = T, and Section 2.3 corrects rendered intervals to start at T. These are limited corrections to the written procedure, consistent with the existing two-stage description; the simulation engine, pseudo-experts and training objectives remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D.3 adds a training condition using lower-fidelity simulations with PSNR < 27, which the standard pipeline excludes. This extends simulated input-quality coverage, while the nuPlan/NAVSIM datasets, navtrain/navhard/navtest coverage and driving task remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The leaderboard comparators and evaluated planner families remain unchanged, including PDM-Closed, LTF, DiffusionDrive and GTRS-Dense. The newly evaluated EgoMLP diagnoses differences between simulated and real data rather than serving as a new comparator against SimScale.

E3.justification: Reported simulation pools increase from 140K to 147K recovery-based scenes and from 185K to 237K planner-based scenes. Appendix D.3 introduces a matched-sample fidelity experiment using approximately 10K samples per round over two rounds. Existing benchmark splits, metrics and model-training hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands diagnostic evidence: Appendix D.2 examines simulated scenario difficulty using EgoMLP, D.3 tests visual fidelity with matched samples, and C.3 extends reactive versus non-reactive comparisons to full scaling curves. It also adds or replaces qualitative cases and revises ensemble results. The varying-real-data analysis already existed in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions describe residual-standard-deviation bands for the least-squares scaling fits in Section 3.3. Neither introduces repeated-run counts, seed reporting, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new performance-distribution plots do not establish a changed uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–4 and 7–9 extensively revise simulated-training results. For example, navhard scores change from 32.8 to 32.6 for DiffusionDrive and from 45.1 to 46.9 and 47.2 to 48.0 for the two GTRS-Dense backbones. These accompany revised simulation pools, so they are not established same-setting gains. Table 9 reverses the six-model ensemble's advantage over the best three-model ensemble. Figure 8 and Table 10 add new difficulty and fidelity findings.

T1.justification: The recovery-matching definition, co-training losses, EPDMS formula and log-quadratic least-squares formulation remain mathematically unchanged in Equations 1–8. No new assumptions, theorems, proofs or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion strengthen the reported maximum navhard improvement from +6.8 to +8.6 EPDMS. The +2.9 navtest claim and central contributions concerning scalable simulation, co-training, exploration and multimodal planners retain their scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation that accumulated visual artifacts can cause performance degradation, interprets the fidelity ablation as evidence of a reduced visual domain gap, and interprets EgoMLP's lower simulation scores as greater scenario difficulty. The revised self-play discussion adds interaction-cost and simulation-fidelity limitations; most existing limitations are retained.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a future code/data-release promise into a reported release with a repository address. V2 also documents sampling for the new fidelity experiment. Existing architecture and training details are largely relocated from Section 3.1 to Appendix B.2, rather than newly disclosed.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including DriveFine, PerLAD and PlannerRFT. Appendix A.4 expands and relocates the earlier online-RL discussion, explicitly positioning SimScale as supporting imitation learning and offline reward learning across planners. Bibliographic updates to existing works do not constitute additional research changes.

P1.justification: V2 makes local wording corrections, adds project-lead attribution, moves model-training paragraphs to the appendix, and reorganizes supplementary experiments into extended and additional results. The introduction, method narrative and overall argument remain largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds an online-RL comparison schematic, reactive-scaling and scenario-distribution plots, Table 10, and two additional qualitative figures. It also revises Figure 5 and appendix scene visualizations. The existing varying-real-data plot is retained as Figure 9 rather than being a new analysis.

improvement.justification: The matched-fidelity ablation, scenario-difficulty analysis and fuller reactive-scaling evidence modestly strengthen validation, while explicit release information improves reproducibility guidance. These benefits are tempered by new numerical inconsistencies: reward-only ResNet34 scores differ between Tables 3 and 7 (45.9 versus 46.9), and V2-99 navtest scores differ between Tables 2 and 8 (84.6 versus 84.8). The net improvement is therefore limited.
